## Method details
 
Initial analysis of the spectral file outputs from the Mass Spectrometer, were processed using `r params$data_type`, which uses a proteomic search engine to perform peptide and protein identifications, and assign intensity values to the identified proteins. Label-free quantification was applied to the intensities and the grouped values were outputted as a table. 

The `r file_input` was uploaded into a web-based analysis suite "SAINT_DEP + Cluster" \textsuperscript{1}, along with experimental design information. "SAINT_DEP + Cluster"  uses a number of R packages to process the protein intensitiy data, and  perform cluster analysis to allow data visualization and discovery of significantly enriched proteins. Briefly the suite uses the "DEP" package \textsuperscript{2} to perform contaminant filtering , normalization and imputation of missing values. Normalization was performed using the variance stabilizing transformation method (vsn) and missing values were imputed using the ‘Missing not At Random’ (MNAR) method, which uses random draws from a left-shifted Gaussian distribution of 1.8 StDev (standard deviation) apart with a width of 0.3. Protein-wise linear models combined with empirical Bayes statistics were used for the differential expression analyses. "DEP" uses the  _limma_ package from R Bioconductor to generate a list of differentially expressed proteins for each chosen pair-wise comparison. A cutoff using the chosen _adjusted p-value_ of `r params$p` (Benjamini-Hochberg method) along with a fold change of `r params$lfc` has been applied to determine a list of significantly regulated proteins in each chosen pairwise comparison. Both the _adjusted p-value_ and fold change can be adjusted interactively and information of the number and percentage of total  of proteins is displayed dynamically. The suite also uses "DEP" to generate Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and correlation plots to evaluate replicate quality. `r second_round_txt`

To identify clusters of proteins Heatmaps are generated using the "ComplexHeatmap package" \textsuperscript{3,4} using the chosen condition comparisons and the protein list generated from the "DEP" package. k-means clustering allows proteins of similar fold change values to be grouped and subjected to GO ontology enrichment analysis using the package "clusterProfiler"\textsuperscript{5}. Enhanced Volcano plots\textsuperscript{6} and box plots are also generated to validate possible proteins of interest.  The suite also has built in SAINTexpress analysis, which allows identification proteins that have a higher abundance compared to the control samples.
 
\textsuperscript{1} SAINT_DEP + Cluster by Stuart Cain (Manuscript in preparation)
\textsuperscript{2} Zhang X, Smits A, van Tilburg G, Ovaa H, Huber W, Vermeulen M (2018). “Proteome-wide identification of ubiquitin interactions using UbIA-MS.” Nature Protocols, 13, 530–550.
\textsuperscript{3}Gu, Z. Complex Heatmap Visualization. iMeta 2022.
\textsuperscript{4} Gu, Z. Complex heatmaps reveal patterns and correlations in multidimensional genomic data. Bioinformatics 2016.
\textsuperscript{5} Blighe, K, S Rana, and M Lewis. 2018. “EnhancedVolcano: Publication-ready volcano plots with enhanced colouring and labeling.” https://github.com/kevinblighe/EnhancedVolcano
\textsuperscript{6} Wu T, Hu E, Xu S, Chen M, Guo P, Dai Z, Feng T, Zhou L, Tang W, Zhan L, Fu x, Liu S, Bo X, Yu G (2021). “clusterProfiler 4.0: A universal enrichment tool for interpreting omics data.” The Innovation, 2(3), 100141. doi:10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100141. `r saint_ref_txt`

## Results

## Summary of parameters used:
* Input Data Type= <span style="color:blue">`r params$data_type`</span>
* Comparison Type= <span style="color:blue">`r params$comp_type`</span>
`r comp_data_text`
* Log fold change cutoff >= <span style="color:blue">`r params$lfc`</span>
* Adjusted _p-value_ cutoff <= <span style="color:blue">`r params$p`</span>  
* Log fold change cutoff 2 >= <span style="color:blue">`r params$lfc2`</span>

* Adjusted _p-value_ cutoff 2 <= <span style="color:blue">`r params$p2`</span>  
* No. of Samples= <span style="color:blue">`r sample_no`</span>




### The result output from `r params$data_type`  contains `r nrow(params$data())` proteins groups of which `r nrow(params$dep())` proteins were reproducibly quantified.
### `r num_signif` proteins differ significantly between samples.

## Missing Value handling

### Missing value heatmap
A heatmap for proteins with missing value in each dataset. Each row represent a protein with missing value in one or more replicate. Each replicate is clustered based on presence of missing values in the sample. 



### Enhanced Volcano Plots
```{r enh_volcano, echo=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE, comment=NA}
      if (params$comp_type == "2 Rounds of comparisons"){
        lfc<-as.numeric(params$lfc2)
        p<-as.numeric(params$p2)
        comp<-params$comp2()              
      }else{lfc<-as.numeric(params$lfc)
      p<-as.numeric(params$p)
      comp<-params$comp()
      }

for(i in comp){
  enh_vol<-plot_enhanced_volcano (params$data_results(),
                               params$cluster_heatmap_input()[[19]],
                               comp_pick = i,
                               FC=lfc,
                               pVal=p,
                               #padj_check="p-adj sig.",
                               padj_check=params$p_adj_enh1,
                               params$colour_functions_input()[[2]],
                               as.numeric(params$colour_functions_input()[[3]])
  )
# print(enh_vol)
  print(i)
}
if (params$rendered_by_shiny)
shiny::setProgress(1)  # set progress to 100%
```
